title: Sugreeva's knowledge of physical world
introduction: Sugreeva's knowledge of physical world is acquired when Vali put him to flight. Rama enquires with Sugreeva as to how Sugreeva has many details of lands, countries, rivers, and mountains. In reply, Sugreeva says that when repulsed by Vali he was on the run to pillar to post, until he finally settled on Mt. Rishyamuka. During such a plighted flight, Sugreeva says, he acquired a direct and personal knowledge of earth.
closing: This and last few chapters that describe the topography and geography of earth may seem redundant or a wasteful narration. No purpose is apparently solved in narrating at such a length and in such vividness, when the main purpose is searching Seetha. Sugreeva might have simply said 'go and search everywhere...' This is as inquired by the commentator of Dharmaakuutam.
na anvatra janaka tanaya gaveṣaṇāya prasthitān vānarān prati prācyādi dikṣu gavesaṇīya pradeśa viśeṣaṇānām viśiṣya kathanam na prayojanavat |

For this it is replied that at the outset of undertaking a high-risk task like the elimination of Ravana, some pious deeds of seeing, hearing, or telling about the pious lands, mountains, rivers, and sages that dwell thereabout, are to be undertaken. A laudatory salutation to Mother Earth is a sacred act. So Sugreeva has earned some merit in eulogising places and sending his troops to all places as a kind of tiirtha yaatra 'a pilgrimage...' as said by the commentator:

saamaanya uktyaa preShaNa sambhavaat iti cet ucyate - prabalatara shatru vadhaaadi mahaa kaaryam saadhayataa prathamataH tasmaat ardha daayakam tapaH caraNa puNya tiirtha kShetra deva brahma raaja R^iShaya samkiirtana shravaNa darshana smaraNaadiShu puNyatameShu yat kimcit kartavyam | sugriiveNa api kimcit puNyam karma kartavyam - puNya desha tiirtha maharShiNaam tat upeta bhuu golasya ca samkiirtana shravaNaadikam prashastam | - This is the same situation when Rama and Lakshmana venerated sapta jana aashrama 'the Seven-Sage's hermitage...' when Sugreeva proceeded with them for attacking Vali, in the second instance, in Kishkindha Ch. 13. Rama was not successful in the first round of attacking Vali, as he venerated none such tutelary in first round.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे षट् चत्वारिन्शः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 46th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
गतेषु वानरेन्द्रेषु रामः सुग्रीवम् अब्रवीत् |
कथम् भवान् विजानीते सर्वम् वै मण्डलम् भुवः
verses.iast:
gateṣu vānarendreṣu rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt |
katham bhavān vijānīte sarvam vai maṇḍalam bhuvaḥ
verses.translation: When the chiefs of monkey-troops are on their way Rama spoke to Sugreeva, "Indeed, how do you know very-well about the globe of earth in its entirety?"

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवः च ततो रामम् उवाच प्रणत आत्मवान् |
श्रूयताम् सर्वम् आख्यास्ये विस्तरेण वचो मम
verses.iast:
sugrīvaḥ ca tato rāmam uvāca praṇata ātmavān |
śrūyatām sarvam ākhyāsye vistareṇa vaco mama
verses.translation: Then Sugreeva bowing down before Rama said, "I will narrate all vividly, and let my words be heard."

verses.devanagari:
यदा तु दुंदुभिम् नाम दानवम् महिष आकृतिम् |
परिकालयते वाली मलयम् प्रति पर्वतम्
तदा विवेश महिषो मलयस्य गुहाम् प्रति |
विवेश वाली तत्र अपि मलयम् तत् जिघांसया
verses.iast:
yadā tu duṃdubhim nāma dānavam mahiṣa ākṛtim |
parikālayate vālī malayam prati parvatam
tadā viveśa mahiṣo malayasya guhām prati |
viveśa vālī tatra api malayam tat jighāṃsayā
verses.translation: "When Vali repulsed the buffalo-shaped demon Dundubhi towards Malaya mountain, then that buffalo entered the cave of Mt. Malaya, and even Vali entered therein wishing to kill that buffalo.
notes: This buffalo-demon Dundubhi was killed by Vali in Kishkindha and its carcass was hurled into the precincts of Sage Matanga's hermitage. While that demon was killed there, Sugreeva is now telling that this demon was killed in a cave. The demon killed in cave was Maayaavi, as said in Ch. 9 of this canto. Maayaavi and Dundubhi are brothers and sons of Maya. Maheshvara Tiirtha says because Dundubhi is the son of buffalo-demon Maya, i.e., Dundubhi Sr., thus he can be called as Dundubhi. And Govindaraja says:

dundubheḥ pūrvajaḥ agrajaḥ sutaḥ mayasya iti seṣaḥ vakṣyatu uttara kāṇḍe mayaḥ - māyāvī prathamaḥ stāt dundubhiḥ tat anantaram iti...'Maayaavi is the first son and the second one is Dundubhi- as said by Maya in Uttara Kanda...' Then it is assumed that both Maayaavi and Dundubhi have come in the first instance for a fight with Vali. But on seeing Vali and Sugreeva, Dundubhi might have entered into the cave with Maayaavi and somehow escaped from there, and thus only Maayaavi is killed by Vali. Later Dundubhi came at the gate of Kishkindha and was killed by Vali. Hence, Sugreeva's referring to Dundubhi here includes both Maayaavi and Dundubhi.

verses.devanagari:
ततो अहम् तत्र निक्षिप्तो गुहा द्वारि विनीतवत् |
न च निष्क्रमते वाली तदा संवत्सरे गते
verses.iast:
tato aham tatra nikṣipto guhā dvāri vinītavat |
na ca niṣkramate vālī tadā saṃvatsare gate
verses.translation: "Vali then kept me at the mouth of the cave as I was an amenable brother, but Vali did not exit from cave even after one full year.

glosses.meaning: Vali, not, out, coming - exiting from cave.

verses.devanagari:
ततः क्षतज वेगेन आपुपूरे तदा बिलम् |
तत् अहम् विस्मितो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातुः शोक विष अर्दितः
verses.iast:
tataḥ kṣataja vegena āpupūre tadā bilam |
tat aham vismito dṛṣṭvā bhrātuḥ śoka viṣa arditaḥ
verses.translation: "I was dumbfounded to see that cave is then fully filled with blood, and then a venom like anguish called the loss of my brother agonised me.

glosses.meaning: for brother's [loss,] anguish, by venom, I was agonised.

verses.devanagari:
अथ अहम् गत बुद्धिः तु सुव्यक्तम् निहतो गुरुः |
शिला पर्वत संकाशा बिल द्वारि मया कृता
अशक्नुवन् निष्क्रमितुम् महिषो विनशिष्यति |
verses.iast:
atha aham gata buddhiḥ tu suvyaktam nihato guruḥ |
śilā parvata saṃkāśā bila dvāri mayā kṛtā
aśaknuvan niṣ.hkramitum mahiṣo vinaśiṣyati |
verses.translation: "Then I concluded that 'my brother is unmistakably killed,' and then I fixed a mountain similar boulder in the mouth of that cavity with a thinking that it will be impossible for that buffalo to exit and it will get destroyed within that cave itself.

glosses.meaning: I, acquired, mind [concluded,] on my part

verses.devanagari:
ततो अहम् आगाम् किष्किंधाम् निराशः तस्य जीविते
राज्यम् च सुमहत् प्राप्य ताराम् च रुमया सह |
मित्रैः च सहितः तत्र वसामि विगत ज्वरः
verses.iast:
tato aham āgām kiṣkiṃdhām nirāśaḥ tasya jīvite
rājyam ca sumahat prāpya tārām ca rumayā saha |
mitraiḥ ca sahitaḥ tatra vasāmi vigata jvaraḥ
verses.translation: "Unhopeful of Vali's aliveness then I arrived in Kishkindha, and on getting the very magnificent kingdom of Kishkindha, and also Ruma along with Tara, I was peaceably staying there with friends.

glosses.meaning: Ruma, along with Lady Tara, also
without, febrility [disquiet, owing to brother's loss, i.e., peaceably]

verses.devanagari:
आजगाम ततो वाली हत्वा तम् दानवर्षभः |
ततो अहम् अददाम् राज्यम् गौरवात् भय यंत्रितः
verses.iast:
ājagāma tato vālī hatvā tam dānavarṣabhaḥ |
tato aham adadām rājyam gauravāt bhaya yaṃtritaḥ
verses.translation: "Vali then came back to Kishkindha on killing that great demon, and then I was spellbound in fear of Vali's killing me, and I gave back the kingdom to Vali owing to my deference to him.

glosses.meaning: him, demon, great one, on killing
owing to deference, kingdom, gave back.

verses.devanagari:
स माम् जिघांसुः दुष्टात्मा वाली प्रव्यथित इन्द्रियः |
परिकालयते क्रोधात् धावंतम् सचिवैः सह
verses.iast:
sa mām jighāṃsuḥ duṣṭātmā vālī pravyathita indriyaḥ |
parikālayate krodhāt dhāvaṃtam sacivaiḥ saha
verses.translation: "That evil-minded Vali becoming highly perturbed at his senses furiously repulsed me further and further away, even though I was running away from him with my ministers, as he wished to kill me.

glosses.meaning: evil, minded one, he that, Vali
ministers, along with, me, while I was running away

verses.devanagari:
ततो अहम् वालिना तेन सानुबन्धः प्रधावितः |
नदीः च विविधाः पश्यन् वनानि नगराणि च
verses.iast:
tato aham vālinā tena sānubandhaḥ pradhāvitaḥ |
nadīḥ ca vividhāḥ paśyan vanāni nagarāṇi ca
verses.translation: "Such as I was, who is repulsed by Vali, I was made to run away rapidly, and during that fleeing I went on seeing diverse rivers, forests and cities.

glosses.meaning: by him, by Vali, pursued - chased
rapidly, made to run away - chased away.

verses.devanagari:
आदर्श तल संकाशा ततो वै पृथिवी मया |
अलात चक्र प्रतिमा दृष्टा गोष्पदवत् तदा - कृता
verses.iast:
ādarśa tala saṃkāśā tato vai pṛthivī mayā |
alāta cakra pratimā dṛṣṭā goṣpadavat tadā - kṛtā
verses.translation: "I have then really seen the earth as in the reflection on the surface of a mirror, where the mirror shows all the objects in exactness, and the earth is like the circle of a fireball, where it is encircled with fire-like reddish, brownish, ochreish minerals and ores, and it appeared to me in my high flight like a cow-hoof-print in the mirror, called my perception.

glosses.meaning: mirror's, surface [reflection on the surface of a mirror,] like
then, analogous to cow-hoof-print, [made as,] indeed.

verses.devanagari:
पूर्वम् दिशाम् ततो गत्वा पश्यामि विविधान् द्रुमान् |
पर्वतान् स दरीन् रम्यान् सरांसि विविधानि च
verses.iast:
pūrvam diśām tato gatvā paśyāmi vividhān drumān |
parvatān sa darīn ramyān sarāṃsi vividhāni ca
verses.translation: "Then on going to eastern direction I saw various trees, enchanting mountains with caves, and also numerous lakes.

verses.devanagari:
उदयम् तत्र पश्यामि पर्वतम् धातु मण्डितम् |
क्षीरोदम् सागरम् चैव नित्यम् अप्सर आलयम्
verses.iast:
udayam tatra paśyāmi parvatam dhātu maṇḍitam |
kśīrodam sāgaram caiva nityam apsara ālayam
verses.translation: "There I saw the mountain wreathed in with ores, namely Mt. Udaya, the Sun-Rise, and I have also seen the Milk Water Oceans which is forever an abode for apsara-s.

verses.devanagari:
परिकाल्यमानः तदा वालिना अभिद्रुतः हि अहम् |
पुनः आवृत्य सहसा प्रस्थितो अहम् तदा विभो
verses.iast:
parikālyamānaḥ tadā vālinā abhidrutaḥ hi aham |
punaḥ āvṛtya sahasā prasthito aham tadā vibho
verses.translation: "I fled speedily when Vali repulsed me, but oh, lord Rama, when I returned he again made me to flee forthwith.

glosses.meaning: by Vali, [again,] made to travel - chased to flee.

verses.devanagari:
दिशः तस्याः ततो भूयः प्रस्थितो दक्षिणम् दिशम् |
विन्ध्य पादप संकीर्णाम् चन्दन द्रुम शोभिताम्
verses.iast:
diśaḥ tasyāḥ tato bhūyaḥ prasthito dakśiṇam diśam |
vindhya pādapa saṅkīrṇām candana druma śobhitām
verses.translation: "Then from that eastern direction I fled to southern direction, which is thick with Vindhya Range mountains and diverse trees, especially with sandalwood trees.

glosses.meaning: [both] Vindhya Range mountains, trees, thick with
to southern, direction, I was fled.

verses.devanagari:
द्रुम शैल अन्तरे पश्यन् भूयो दक्षिणतो अपराअम् |
अपराम् च दिशम् प्राप्तो वालिना समभिद्रुतः
verses.iast:
druma śaila antare paśyan bhūyo dakśiṇato aparāam |
aparām ca diśam prāpto vālinā samabhidrutaḥ
verses.translation: "While I was seeing the interiors of forest and mountains again I was made to run by Vali, who was setting upon me from within the interiors of those forests and mountains, and then I reached the western direction.

glosses.meaning: again, by Vali, made to run
western, direction, I reached. [Here aparaam means doubly 1. another, 2. west quarter.]

verses.devanagari:
स पश्यन् विविधान् देशान् अस्तम् च गिरि सत्तमम् |
प्राप्य च अस्तम् गिरि श्रेष्ठम् उत्तरम् संप्रधावितः
verses.iast:
sa paśyan vividhān deśān astam ca giri sattamam |
prāpya ca astam giri śreṣṭham uttaram sampradhāvitaḥ
verses.translation: "Such as I was, on seeing diverse cities and the best mountain Astagiri, Mt. Dusk, I reached that excellent Mt. Dusk also, and since Vali is at my heel, I took to my heels, by a long way to north.

glosses.meaning: mountain, excellent one, Mt. Dusk, also
very, much [by a long way,] ran [took to my heels.]

verses.devanagari:
हिमवंतम् च मेरुम् च समुद्रम् च तथा उत्तरम् |
यदा न विन्दे शरणम् वालिना समभिद्रुतः
ततो माम् बुद्धि संपन्नो हनुमान् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
himavaṃtam ca merum ca samudram ca tathā uttaram |
yadā na vinde śaraṇam vālinā samabhidrutaḥ
tato mām buddhi sampanno hanumān vākyam abravīt |
verses.translation: "Even at Himalayas, Mt. Meru, like that at the Northern Ocean, Vali drove me back, and when the clemency from Vali, or a shelter, or even a foothold on earth was indeterminable, then Hanuma, whose prosperity is his wisdom, said a word to me.

glosses.meaning: by Vali, driven back [even from north]
shelter [or clemency from Vali, or, foothold on earth
not, known - I could not see, or get

verses.devanagari:
इदानीम् मे स्मृतम् राजन् यथा वाली हरीश्वरः
मतंगेन तदा शप्तो हि अस्मिन् आश्रम मण्डले |
प्रविशेत् यदि वै वाली मूर्धा अस्य शतधा भवेत्
तत्र वासः सुखो अस्माकम् निर्उद्विग्नो भविष्यति |
verses.iast:
idānīm me smṛtam rājan yathā vālī harīśvaraḥ
mataṃgena tadā śapto hi asmin āśrama maṇḍale |
praviśet yadi vai vālī mūrdhā asya śatadhā bhavet
tatra vāsaḥ sukho asmākam nir.hudvigno bhaviṣyati |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, king Sugreeva, now I remember how Sage Matanga cursed the king of monkeys Vali at that time. If Vali really enters the fringes of the hermitage of Sage Matanga, Vali's head gets splintered in hundred ways. Hence dwelling in sage Matanga's hermitage will be peaceful and imperturbable for us.' Thus Hanuma spoke to me.

glosses.meaning: by Sage Matanga, as to how, cursed, indeed
to me, now, came to remembrance
Vali, in that [Matanga's,] hermitage, in fringes
his [Vali's,] head, in hundred ways, becomes [splinters - Vali's head gets splintered]

verses.devanagari:
ततः पर्वतम् आसाद्य ऋश्यमूकम् नृपात्मज
न विवेश तदा वाली मतंगस्य भयात् तदा |
एवम् मया तदा राजन् प्रत्यक्षम् उपलक्षितम् |
पृथिवी मण्डलम् सर्वम् गुहाम् अस्मि आगतः ततः
verses.iast:
tataḥ parvatam āsādya ṛśyamūkam nṛpātmaja
na viveśa tadā vālī mataṃgasya bhayāt tadā |
evam mayā tadā rājan pratyakṣam upalakṣitam |
pṛthivī maṇḍalam sarvam guhām asmi āgataḥ tataḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, prince Rama, then Vali though reached Mt. Rishyamuka, he did not enter into its precincts at that time fearing Sage Matanga and his curse, oh, king Rama, thus this globe of earth is apparently and closely sighted by me in its entirety, and then I came into the cave of Rishyamuka and did not stir out." So said Sugreeva to Rama.

glosses.meaning: then, not, entered - came to mountain
to cave, came, I am - I have come to the cave of Rishyamuka.
